question: True or false: in blind trials, leading violin soloists reliably picked out Stradivari and other old Italian violins from new ones?
answer: False. Claudia Fritz's team had ten soloists play six old Italian and six new violins in goggles that hid the instruments. Six of the ten chose a new violin as the one to take on tour, and they could not tell old from new better than chance. Fame and price had been doing the hearing.
move: Hide the label, then check whether the preference survives.
ask: Which of my favourite brands would I still choose if the label were hidden?
trap: Assuming instruments costing millions must sound better to experts.
reference: Fritz et al., Soloist evaluations of six Old Italian and six new violins, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2014
